cue_frames.caption_text: On Mapping, read the warehouse call label and open description
before interpreting the marker.
That popup identifies a fictional incident; it does not establish
where a person or apparatus is now.
This walkthrough reviews Core administration and recorded training data.
Device permissions and field tracking need their own application checks.
Keep that distinction visible when using location information for fire and EMS,
community response, or industrial standby.
In Department Settings, review Address and Default Map Center GPS Coordinates.
The paired latitude and longitude inputs describe the starting map
view, not a live vehicle fix.
This example uses a fictional Chicago address and explicit decimal coordinates.
Check Street, City, State/Province, Zip/Postal Code and Country
before relying on the extent.
Save and Cancel are visible; this demonstration reads existing values
and leaves the department unchanged.
On Edit Group, confirm Station Group and Group Name before reading Station Address.
Firehouse 51 has a fictional Chicago address and Gps Coordinates; the lower
what3words Address field is empty.
These are alternative station-location inputs, not a live fix.
Group Boundary is a separate response or service area.
This demonstration reads the existing fields and preserves the station,
boundary, apparatus assignment and crew.
On Mapping, use Filter marker text to focus the display.
The retained Truck 81 view leaves that named marker visible.
Show calls, Show stations, Show units, Show personnel and Show
POIs control displayed categories.
In the comparison view, the text filter is empty and Show units is unchecked.
A hidden category is not a released resource or deleted position.
Inspect these controls before treating an expected resource as missing.
From Mapping, Map Icon Legend explains type and priority conventions.
Routine, Urgent and Emergency appear in separate columns.
On Edit Call Type, the Structure Fire Preview shows a stored custom icon and
says Showing the current custom icon.
The warehouse popup supplies the incident description.
These are visual identifiers.
They do not establish a fresh position, response acceptance
or notification receipt.
Read the label and context rather than relying only on
a flame or vehicle picture.
On Mapping, the footer says Last update.
It records when the client loaded or refreshed marker data, or
handled a location update; it is not every resource’s fix time.
In Units, Status and Timestamp belong to the latest unit status.
That time is not a GPS measurement either.
These screens show historical training states.
Check the appropriate position source and age before treating a
page refresh or status entry as evidence that an apparatus moved.
In the recorded New Call position popup, Engine 51 explicitly says
Station location and shows station coordinates beside the call location.
That comparison uses a stored origin.
A unit in quarters, or one without an available live position, can
be measured from its station under the response-origin rules.
Read the source before using the estimate.
The displayed distance and time do not prove physical presence, arrival,
or an active navigation route.
On New Call, compare the Personnel rows.
One historical training view shows Live GPS with a stale badge; the separately
simulated newer view omits that badge.
Live GPS names the application’s data-source category.
No real device permission or physical movement was exercised.
Status, Staffing, ETA and Position are separate columns.
Treat No position as missing information, and review the source and configuration
before using the first ranked candidate as an operational recommendation.
In Mapping and BigBoard Settings, review personnel and unit controls separately.
TTL In Minutes for Personnel Locations
and TTL In Minutes for Unit Locations
both show zero in these views.
Zero disables ping expiry; the help text’s sixty-minute example is not a saved sixty.
A location-bearing status can remain a fallback after a ping expires.
The separate no-location-status checkboxes affect replacement behavior.
Check the policy and position source before promising that
a marker will disappear.
In dispatch settings, Closest Unit Response Tuning has separate age controls.
Maximum unit location age and Maximum personnel location age are in seconds;
both recorded values are eighteen hundred.
They differ from map TTL measured in minutes.
Include stale locations is unchecked.
Maximum response radius is zero, meaning no configured maximum radius.
These controls influence candidate evaluation.
They do not certify a fresh fix, prove service-area coverage,
or change a resource position because the map refreshed.
In the same Closest Unit Response Tuning section, Order by driving ETA is
unchecked and ETA shortlist size is five.
Turnout is one hundred twenty seconds in quarters, zero mobile and zero personnel.
The matching Engine 51 station popup shows a two-minute estimate including
one hundred twenty seconds of turnout.
Response combines applicable turnout with estimated travel.
Routed drive time is separate.
This is no tested drive, confirmed dispatch receipt, physical
movement or arrival commitment.
From Mapping, Manage POIs
opens the empty POI-type list.
In Weather Alerts, Monitoring Zones offers Center Location, Radius in miles
and Save Zone; no zone is saved here.
Hospitals, layers, floor plans and patrol routes still require
their own saved-workflow checks.
For search and rescue, security, wildland or community teams,
apply the same source-and-age checks before operational use.
Keep missing reference data on the follow-up list until its placement
and limits are actually reviewed.
